title: Batchsmith: workload profiling, heuristic recommendations, and safe config rollouts for continuous batching
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Customers run inference workloads with wildly different request shapes. Static batching configs are either too conservative (wasted cost) or too aggressive (latency spikes and regressions). Goal: build a profiling + heuristic recommendation engine ("Batchsmith") that automatically suggests and safely applies batching and caching parameters per model and route, and can continuously tune these settings with controlled rollouts and automatic rollback on regression.

Scope: workload profiling (sequence length histograms, prefix reuse, arrival inter-arrival distribution, concurrency patterns), heuristic rule engine for initial suggestions (batch size targets, batch timeout, KV cache policies, prefix cache TTL), simulation and replay harness to estimate cost/latency trade-offs, safe apply mechanism (shadow apply, canary, staged ramp with health gates), automated rollback and persisted audit trail. Not in scope: model architecture changes, cross-region routing policy changes (handled by Smart Routing team).

Success metrics: token-cost reduction (estimated cost per 1M tokens) >= 8% on typical workloads, p95 latency regressions <= 5% during rollout, KV cache hit increase >= 10% where applicable, zero customer-facing errors from the rollout path.

Design highlights: 1) Profiling agent collects per-route sample windows (5–15 minutes) including sequence-length histogram, prefix fingerprint rates, KV cache hit/miss counters, cold-start counts, arrival interquartiles, and request concurrency snapshots. 2) Heuristic engine maps profiles to a ranked set of candidate configs and an estimated score (cost delta vs latency delta). 3) Simulation runner replays sampled traces against candidate configs to estimate real-world token batching behavior and tail latency impacts. 4) Safe deploy pipeline: a shadow trial phase (traffic mirrored to a test pool), then canary at 1–5% traffic with strict SLO-based gates (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, tokens/sec), followed by gradual ramp if gates pass. 5) Automatic rollback rules and a human-notify escalation - if any gate fails the rollout aborts and rollback executes with a post-mortem entry. 6) Telemetry and explainability: every recommendation stores the fingerprinted profile, confidence score, simulation artifacts, and an easy-to-read rationale for PMs/SEs.

Trade-offs considered: - Aggressive batching improves unit cost but increases tail latency for latency-sensitive routes; we mitigate by conservative latency gates and per-route SLAs. - Simulation fidelity vs performance: keep a bounded sampling window for replay to keep compute costs acceptable. - Applying per-model vs per-route configs: prefer route-level for quick wins, but enable model-family templates for consistency.

Deliverables: profiling agent, heuristic engine service, simulation harness, safe-deploy orchestration (integrates with console rollout UI), rollbacks/audit logs, doc + runbook, e2e tests and load-test scenarios.
